dedupe_keys.name: china msw incineration plant automatic monitoring data disclosure platform and national incinerator database

description: China requires every municipal solid waste incineration power plant to publish its automatic monitoring data, and this national platform shows them: for each plant and incinerator, the previous day's daily averages of particulates, nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride, the furnace temperature curve and data flags, published every day since 2 January 2020. A companion research database, released with a 2026 Nature Communications study, covers 975 plants with 2,151 incinerators and their electricity generation in 2023 (up to 7 percent of residential electricity use), incinerator energy efficiency, and projections to 2035. The platform follows rules of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, with each plant responsible for its data; the database comes from the study's authors. Coverage is national at plant level. The platform is a free web query in Chinese; the database and models are Excel and text files on figshare under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Caveats: platform data are self-reported and flagged by operators, plants that stop reporting show history only, there is no bulk download, and the study's efficiency tiers are modelled. Simulation uses: waste-to-energy capacity and operations for waste system capacity planning, interdependency of waste and electricity supply, and emissions scenarios. Related records: EDGAR-FOOD (data-edgar-food) and the global waste sector projections (data-global-waste-sector-1990-2050).
